anchor_frame: X0 = branch start row 0 aligned into the X_t frame by the fixed S/W weighted Kabsch using only X0 and X_t (feature-lane concern; recorded here)
input_frame: causal current frame X_t: the native branch frame as stored, no future alignment of any kind
interpolation: piecewise-linear on aligned Cartesian coordinates per segment; segments include the first [X_t, Y_{t+1}]; no rotation interpolation, no Cartesian cubic spline, no SLERP

kabsch.convention: row vectors; C=(Y-muY)^T W (X-muX)=U S V^T

label_frame: X_t frame; future frames Y[j] are aligned into X_t with the SAME fixed branch S/W on the label side only, then interpolated piecewise-linearly
no_future_step: a start row whose entire future is identical to X_t within 1e-9 gets no MOVE label (reason no_future_step); STOP is never fabricated

reference_policy.gate: lambda1 > 0.01 A^2 and lambda2/lambda1 > 1e-3 on the start-frame scatter; planar references allowed (no third-eigenvalue requirement); failure -> gauge_unresolved, never a global axis fallback
reference_policy.native_verified_v1: branches whose every tier fails the scatter gate may keep the archive's unified Cartesian frame INSTEAD of Kabsch alignment, only after verify_frame_continuity passes the pre-registered thresholds (consecutive rotation <= 2.0 deg, translation <= 0.10 A; cumulative <= 10.0 deg / 1.0 A); evidence per branch in the native sidecar; failing branches stay gauge_unresolved (plan §1.3)
reference_policy.set: start-endpoint non-key heavy atoms within 1-2 covalent hops of the key set, in the rigid block(s) after cutting non-ring single bonds with both endpoints degree>=2
reference_policy.tiered_fallback: rigid_1_2hop -> any_1_2hop -> any_3hop -> all_nonkey_heavy (plan §1.3 candidate-block distance/size rule); first tier passing the scatter gate wins; per-branch tier and all tier gates recorded in the native sidecar
reference_policy.weights: w_i = [i in S] / (1 + hop(i,A))^2; W = diag(w/sum w)

root_finding.contact: per segment solve sum_i ||y_i(a)-x_i||^2 = d0^2; earliest root in [0,1] along the path; float64
